content.learning_goal: Teach learners to understand and apply the main ideas of 'Far and Near'.

explanation_sections.title: Connect
explanation_sections.explanation: Begin with learners' prior experience related to Far and Near and invite predictions.

explanation_sections.title: Explore
explanation_sections.explanation: Use the chapter evidence below to build the explanation rather than introducing unsupported facts.
source_evidence: 55 ChapterChapter Far and Near Identify the appropriate units for measuring each of the following.
We have learnt about measuring length and some standard units we use to measure length.
In this chapter we will learn some more units of measuring distances and the relationships between different units.

Let Us Find Quantity Unit of measurement Metre (m) or centimetre (cm) Height of India Gate 42 Length of a handkerchief 40 Depth of a well 50 Length of a mobile phone 13 Length of an elephant’s trunk 2 Distance between two buttons on a shirt 5 Shikha and Sonu are measuring the lengths of saris and stoles in the village weaving centre.

explanation_sections.title: Make meaning
explanation_sections.explanation: Ask learners to explain what the evidence shows, compare ideas, and justify answers.

explanation_sections.title: Apply
explanation_sections.explanation: Move from a chapter example to a new, closely related example.

teaching_sequence.teacher_action: Model close reading/working with the chapter.

teaching_sequence.student_action: Explain why an answer is supported.

misconceptions: Giving an answer without explaining the reasoning.
checks_for_understanding: What evidence in 'Far and Near' supports your answer?
Can you explain the idea in your own words?
content.closure: Ask the learner to state the most important idea and one way it can be used.
